fields.meta_description: Build a business landing page for quotes, wholesale orders, bookings or catering, with every inquiry saved to a database you own. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Business Landing Page That Captures Every Inquiry
fields.hero_description: Build a business landing page that asks for one thing, sends each inquiry to the right person, and keeps it in your own database.
fields.features_heading: What Goes Into a Business Landing Page
fields.features_subheading: A business landing page is one page built for one action, such as a quote or a booking. These six parts get each inquiry answered.
fields.feature_1:
Describe the business, get the page

Tell Emergent what you sell and the one thing the page should ask visitors for. It builds the page and the table that stores each answer, then changes any part when you prompt again.
fields.feature_2:
One page, one action

Pick the action the page exists for: a quote, an order estimate, a booking, or an inquiry. The headline and the button both point at that action, with no menu pulling visitors away.
fields.feature_3:
Every inquiry is a row you own

Each submission saves as a row in a database you own, with every answer in its own column. Sort quote requests by due date or filter bookings by week without searching an inbox.
fields.feature_4:
Big inquiries reach the right person

Set a rule on any answer, such as a quantity over 1,000, and the app sends a Slack, email, or in-app alert to the person who handles it. Inquiries under the line wait in the table.
fields.feature_5:
New inquiries sync to your CRM

Connect the page to HubSpot or any other tool with an API, and each new inquiry syncs across as it arrives. Sales picks up the lead in the tool it already opens every morning.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain now, your code later

Publish on the domain your business already uses; custom domains are included and use credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and keep building.

fields.usecase_heading: Business Landing Page Examples by Goal
fields.tab_content_1:
Each quote request arrives with the quantity and due date

Pellbury Print Works prints packaging for shops. Its quote page asks how many pieces are needed and by what date. Halloway Market asked for 2,500 tote bags by November 20, and its request saved as one of 38 quote requests this week, sorted by due date.
fields.tab_content_2:
$690 a week, shown before the cafe writes in

Wrenhaven Coffee Roasters sells beans to cafes. Its wholesale page asks how many pounds a cafe goes through each week and multiplies that by the $11.50 wholesale price per pound. Rook Hollow Cafe entered 60 lb, saw $690 a week, and sent its inquiry with the estimate saved beside it.
fields.tab_content_3:
Only open times are offered for a call

Merrowfield Accounting gives new clients a free 30-minute call. Its page lists the times still open, and a time drops off the list once someone books it. Nadia Prewitt of Cindervale Florist took 10:30 AM on October 28, one of 14 calls booked this week, and her confirmation went to her inbox.
fields.tab_content_4:
Ines Vallort hears when 50 or more guests are coming

Quenby Bakehouse caters office lunches and asks for the company name and the guest count. An order for 50 guests or more sends owner Ines Vallort a Slack message with the company name and the count. Fairhollow Architects asked for 80 guests, and every inquiry still saves as a row.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Business Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Follow seven steps to create a business landing page that asks for one action and gets every inquiry to the right person.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pick the one action the page asks for
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Write the headline as the result
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Ask only what the reply needs
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Describe the page in a prompt
fields.howto_step_1_des: Choose whether the page exists to collect quote requests or to book calls, and write that action down in one sentence before anything else. Every later choice, from the headline to the form fields, gets checked against that sentence.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Name what the visitor walks away with, such as a printed quote for 2,500 tote bags, rather than the company name or a slogan. Put the supporting detail in one short line under it, and use the same words on the button.
fields.howto_step_3_des: List the answers someone needs before replying, such as a quantity, a date, or a guest count, and cut every other field. A name and an email are enough to reply; leave the phone number out unless the first contact is a call.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Name the business, the action, each field, and what should happen after a submission. Emergent builds the page from that prompt. Read the first draft against your one-sentence action from step 01, and prompt again wherever the page drifts from it.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Set who hears about which inquiries
fields.howto_step_5_des: Decide which inquiries need a person right away, such as an order over a set quantity, and name that person. Add the rule to your prompt and say whether that person should get a Slack message or an email.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Send a test inquiry down every path
fields.howto_step_6_des: Submit one inquiry that should trigger each rule and one that should not. Check that each lands as a row with every answer in the right column, and that each alert reaches the right person with the details needed to reply.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Publish and read the first week
fields.howto_step_7_des: Connect your domain and publish. Through the first week, read each inquiry as it arrives and note the fields people skip or misread. Rewrite those fields with another prompt instead of waiting for a full redesign of the page.

faq_plan.q: What is a landing page for a company?
faq_plan.ref: What is a landing page for a company?

prov.original: What is a landing page for a company?

faq_plan.a: A landing page for a company is a single web page built to get visitors to take one action, such as requesting a quote or booking a call. It leaves off the site menu and the other offers a homepage carries. Point one ad or email at a business landing page, and write it for the people that source sends.

faq_plan.q: How to design a company landing page?
faq_plan.ref: How to design a company landing page?

prov.original: How to design a company landing page?

faq_plan.a: Start from the one action you want and design down from it. Write a headline that names what the visitor gets, add a line of proof, keep the form to the fields a reply needs, and end on one button. Leave the site menu off. To skip the template, describe the page to Emergent's AI landing page builder, which creates the page and its database table from your prompt.

faq_plan.q: How many calls to action should landing pages for business have?
faq_plan.a: One. Give the page a single action and repeat that same button lower down for visitors who scroll. If the business has two offers, such as bulk quotes and a free consultation, build two pages and send each audience to its own.

faq_plan.q: How is a landing page for business buyers different from one for consumers?
faq_plan.a: It asks for more and ends in a conversation instead of a checkout. A consumer page can close with a purchase, while a b2b landing page closes with a quote request or a booked sales call. Ask for company size or quantity, and answer the questions a purchasing manager would raise before they reach out.

faq_plan.q: When is a business landing page template the right starting point?
faq_plan.a: When your page matches the template's layout closely and the form needs few changes. Describe the page from scratch when your fields or your follow-up differ, and check any template for what happens after the button is clicked. Emergent builds the page from a description, and the same prompt sets the fields and what happens after each submission.

faq_plan.q: What should a company landing page template include?
faq_plan.a: It should include a headline slot, a line for supporting detail, a place for proof such as a client count or a review, a short form, and a single button. Before you pick one, check that you can remove the site menu and change the form fields, since those two decide whether visitors act.

faq_plan.q: When should one business landing page become two?
faq_plan.a: Split it whenever the action or the audience changes. A printer taking bulk quotes and hosting a trade-show demo day needs two: the quote page asks for quantity and due date, while the event landing page asks for a time slot and a headcount. Keeping them apart shows which source brought in which inquiry.

faq_plan.q: What fields should a business landing page form ask for?
faq_plan.a: Ask for a way to reply, such as an email, plus the one or two answers that shape your reply, such as an event date or an order size. Leave out anything you could look up later. Pages Emergent builds save each answer as its own column in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: How do I measure whether a business landing page is working?
faq_plan.a: Divide inquiries by visitors for the inquiry rate, and track it separately for each traffic source. Then follow the inquiries forward: how many got a reply within a day, and how many turned into paying customers. Change one element at a time, such as the headline, and compare the next month with the last.

faq_plan.q: Should a business landing page promote the whole company or one product?
faq_plan.a: Promote one product or one offer per page. A page about the whole company reads like a homepage and gives visitors no single thing to do. When the page sells one item, a product landing page fits, with the price and a buy button. Emergent builds each page from its own prompt; a second offer takes one more description.

plan.angle: No top 10 in the workbook (Wave 3); the PAA tree shows searchers asking what a company landing page is, how to design one, and about templates and examples. Template galleries show a pretty page and stop at the button. This page wins by showing four business landing pages by the action they ask for (a quote request, a wholesale order estimate, a consultation booking, a catering inquiry) and what happens after the visitor submits: the row it saves, the number it computes, the time it books, the person it alerts. The FAQ answers the definition, the design question, templates, how many actions a page should ask for, and when a business needs more than one page. B2B, service and local business pages are siblings and stay out of the headings.
